title: From Zero to Copilot Agent Builder
description: A first independent MSkill learning journey, not an official Microsoft syllabus.

stages.title: Understand AI basics
exit_criteria: Explain a basic generative AI use case and one limitation.
stages.why: Start with a vocabulary you can question, before choosing a tool.
objectives: Distinguish a generative AI use case from an automated workflow.
Describe a prompt and a limitation you would check.
checkpoints: Write a two-sentence explanation for a colleague. Add one example of an answer you would verify.

resources.title: Introduction to AI concepts
resources.note: Start here. Microsoft describes machine-learning familiarity as helpful, not required.

resources.title: Introduction to generative AI and agents
resources.note: Continue when comfortable with AI terminology. Microsoft lists basic AI and machine-learning familiarity as prerequisites.

stages.title: Map the business problem
exit_criteria: Describe the user, question types and success criteria.
stages.why: A small, explicit problem gives your learning project a useful boundary.
objectives: Name the intended user and the task they need help with.
Define an in-scope question, an out-of-scope question and a success criterion.
checkpoints: Draft a fictional help-desk brief: audience, three questions, information allowed, and one measurable success criterion.

resources.title: Plan your Copilot Studio projects, an overview
resources.note: Read the planning overview and follow the objectives and success criteria guidance.

stages.title: Discover Copilot Studio
exit_criteria: Describe how the agent accesses curated knowledge.
stages.why: Explore the relationship between an agent and the information it is allowed to use.
objectives: Locate the agent creation and testing steps in the official quickstart.
Explain which curated information your fictional agent may use.
checkpoints: Follow the quickstart in an authorized practice environment with synthetic information. Record the intended knowledge source and an expected answer. Without access, make a clearly labelled design walkthrough.

resources.title: Quickstart: Create and deploy an agent with the standard harness
resources.note: Check current access and licensing requirements. A trial permits creation and testing but not publishing. Publishing is not required for this MSkill checkpoint.

stages.title: Connect a safe workflow
exit_criteria: Explain which actions require human review and why.
stages.why: Separating a proposed action from permission to perform it makes a workflow easier to review.
objectives: Sketch a trigger, an action and the connection each needs.
Identify where a person should review a consequential action in your example.
checkpoints: Draw a fictional request-to-reminder flow. Mark its input, connections, expected output and a human review point. Use demo accounts only if trying the official exercise.

resources.title: Get started with Power Automate
resources.note: The module lists Power Automate sign-up and OneDrive for work or school as prerequisites. Read or sketch first if you do not have an authorized practice environment.

stages.title: Understand permissions and governance
exit_criteria: List data access and sharing checks.
stages.why: Decide who should see information before sharing an agent or a workflow.
objectives: List the data and identities involved in your example.
Find the official governance guidance relevant to access and sharing.
checkpoints: Write a short access review for your fictional project: intended users, permitted data, owner, sharing boundary and an unresolved question for an administrator.

resources.title: Key concepts - Copilot Studio security and governance
resources.note: Read the overview and consult the linked controls relevant to your environment. This checkpoint is not a security certification.

stages.title: Ship the first mission
exit_criteria: Run three test scenarios and document results.
stages.why: A small set of recorded examples makes limitations visible and gives you a starting point for improvement.
objectives: Compare expected and observed behavior across three scenarios.
Record one limitation and one improvement for a later version.
checkpoints: Run a normal question, an out-of-scope request and a missing-information case against your practice agent. Record expected and actual results. If using a design walkthrough, label these as simulated rather than executed.

resources.title: Test your agent
resources.note: Use the official test-panel guidance with synthetic data. Keep your observations locally; MSkill does not collect or assess them.
